Survivors of a 2019 landslide in Bududa, an eastern Uganda district prone to landslides, have taken their case to the United Nations Human Rights Committee. The complainants number more than 50 killed, including 33 children, though the article reports two slightly different death tolls: one passage cites 'more than 50 people' and another specifies 'more than 53 people.' Forty-eight survivors filed complaints accusing the government of violating Uganda's constitution by failing to implement effective disaster management measures in Bududa. They argue that a relocation programme ignores their safety, land rights, and livelihoods.

The case is believed to be the first seeking climate adaptation measures globally, potentially setting precedent. Survivors say every heavy rain brings renewed fear of another tragedy; William Tsama, one claimant who lost four family members, framed his legal action as a lesson for victims ignored by governments. Uganda introduced a resettlement plan in 2011 with limited progress, and last month launched a new programme offering affected households 18 million Ugandan shillings ($4,300) to relocate.

Under the scheme, families can choose between two acres of land valued at 8 million shillings ($1,900), plus 10 million shillings (about $2,400) toward building a house, or take the equivalent land allowance in cash alongside the same housing grant. The programme is expected to benefit 1,410 households identified as living in high-risk areas.

The government has given residents of designated high-risk areas two months, from November to December, to leave or face forced eviction. Complainants say changing rainfall patterns and declining soil fertility have also damaged farming livelihoods. They seek compensation for lost family members and livelihoods, plus emergency measures including accessible early-warning systems in high-risk areas.

Survivors first launched legal action in 2020 and received support from the Ugandan environmental organisation Greenwatch three years later. Greenwatch Executive Director Samantha Atukunda Kakuru Mwesigwa said the case is about forcing government policy to keep pace with a changing climate, ensuring loss and damage is no longer an afterthought.

The article places Bududa within broader East African disaster trends: Kenya's floods and landslides killed at least 181 people between March and May 2024 per the Kenya Red Cross; Rwanda's floods and landslides killed 135 in May 2023; and a flash flood swept through Nepal's Gorkha district after a landslide blocked a river, killing over 1,500. ClientEarth lawyer Vesselina Newman said poorer countries contributing little to global emissions bear heavy consequences and need greater financial support from high-income nations.

The UN Human Rights Committee will ask the Ugandan government to respond within six months.
items.title: Uganda landslide survivors seek climate justice at UN

items.summary: Senegalese authorities are continuing search operations after a pirogue reportedly carrying around 100 migrants capsized off the coast near Yenne, south of Dakar. The vessel washed ashore badly damaged on Wednesday and was due to resume searches Thursday. Initial reports said one person had died, though local media reported at least four bodies recovered; dozens remain missing. Oumar Sow, a representative of the village chief, told AFP that cries could be heard from the boat even from the beach around 02:00 GMT. A survivor questioned by police said there were about 100 people aboard, including five women. Police recovered identity documents, several mobile phones and personal belongings, including a school enrolment document. This incident comes less than two weeks after a shipwreck off Thieppe killed at least 39 people in one of Senegal's deadliest migration disasters. At a cabinet meeting Wednesday, President Diomaye Faye expressed concern about renewed irregular departures by migrants hoping to reach Europe and instructed the interior ministry to prepare a report examining the factors driving these journeys and proposing measures to address them; he had previously urged citizens not to risk their lives on such crossings. The UN's IOM recorded at least 454 deaths and disappearances off the West African coast this year, warning the figure likely underestimates reality as many boats vanish without survivors or a trace. As North Africa routes tighten due to stronger European cooperation, migrants are increasingly targeting Spain's Canary Islands in overloaded wooden pirogues unsuited to long Atlantic voyages; most arrivals there this year are from Senegal, driven by limited employment, family pressures and established migration networks. On 7 November, El Hierro declared a state of emergency after more than 3,300 people arrived in about 30 boats since the month began, roughly a third of the island's population.
items.title: Migrant boat capsizes off Senegal, dozens missing

items.summary: A Singapore court sentenced 44-year-old Christopher Sebastian Bland to two days' jail and a S$3,000 fine (US$2,329) after he slapped a woman's buttocks at a nightclub. The prosecutor called the venue "a significant aggravating factor" and urged deterrence, noting public entertainment outlets were the third most common location for molestation in 2025. Four criminal lawyers explained that Singapore law has no fixed rule making a nightclub setting aggravating on its own; courts instead assess whether the offender deliberately exploited the environment or victim's vulnerability. In an earlier case involving oil trader Arrica Frank, jailed one week for slapping a woman at a dimly lit venue where detection is difficult, prosecutors argued he consciously chose to approach and stay near her victim. Prosecutors often cite crime statistics to support deterrence: 1,531 molestation cases were reported in 2025, up 104 from the previous year, with 115 at public entertainment outlets after residential premises and public transport. Mark Yeo of Fortress Law noted it was unclear whether Bland's judge accepted that a nightclub setting is aggravating, as reported reasons focused on the slap itself degrading the victim beyond a mere touch, plus Bland drinking beforehand and denying the offence afterwards. Parliament raised the maximum penalty for outrage of modesty under Section 354(1) of the Penal Code from two years to three years' jail effective Mar 1, 2022. Certain locations are treated more seriously: public transport because it is common and hard to catch; homes, where people should feel safe; hospitals, nursing homes, schools and workplaces; and lifts under Section 354A, which prescribes two to 10 years' jail plus caning if a person is wrongfully restrained. Molestation in a lift or against victims below 14 carries three to 10 years' jail with caning, while Section 354(1) allows up to three years' jail, a fine, caning, or combinations. Judges determine aggravating versus mitigating factors through legislation and parliamentary debates plus prior High Court or Court of Appeal judgments, though the judge ultimately decides what counts rather than prosecutors. Courts cannot double-count factors: if an element like molesting someone under 14 raises the maximum penalty as a statutory aggravator, that same factor is generally not cited again unless the victim is significantly below the prescribed age. Aggravating factors split into offence-specific elements such as prolonged or skin-to-skin contact with private parts, intoxication, deception, abuse of position and violence, plus offender-specific ones like past convictions, similar charges under consideration, victim-blaming and lack of remorse. Victim age and harm suffered, including emotional or psychological trauma, are also weighed. Mitigating factors include early pleas of guilt, one-off incidents, cooperation during investigations, low re-offending risk and professionally assessed mental conditions reducing culpability; remorse, clean records, cooperation and compensation can lower sentences too. Johannes Hadi noted being drunk is not an excuse and counted against Bland. Sentencing remains highly fact-sensitive, with no two cases identical.
items.title: Singapore sentencing factors for molestation offences

items.summary: Tech billionaire Peter Thiel, founder of PayPal and Palantir, has increased his investments in Argentina through additional purchases in Vista Energy, the largest oil exporter operating in Vaca Muerta, a shale formation in Patagonia. According to U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filings reviewed by EL PAÍS USA Edition, Thiel acquired shares through his firm Thiel Macro LLC, which now owns 1,886,835 shares of Vista Energy valued at $123 million. In the second quarter, Thiel Macro added 1,189,792 shares—equivalent to 1% of the company—for nearly $76 million; its stake then rose 58.5% in the third quarter to reach 1,886,835 shares. As a result, Amazon and Vista Energy are now Thiel Macro's two largest holdings, each valued at roughly $123 million and together accounting for nearly 27% of the firm's portfolio. The article notes that Thiel has openly expressed ideological affinity with ultra-conservative Argentine President Javier Milei, arrived in Argentina this year, purchased a mansion in Buenos Aires, and met with Milei both in Los Angeles in 2024 and at Casa Rosada during his visit. With a fortune estimated above $23 billion, the piece frames Thiel as one of the world's richest individuals whose interest in Argentina has grown since Milei took office. Vista Energy was founded in 2017 by engineer Miguel Galuccio—the former chief executive of state-run oil company YPF—along with partners, and it reported net profits of $293.5 million in the third quarter; Vaca Muerta is described as home to the world's second-largest reserves of unconventional natural gas and fourth-largest reserves of shale oil. The article also reports that other U.S. billionaires are increasing their Argentine oil holdings: Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office LLC acquired 403,000 shares of YPF in the last quarter to raise its stake to 3,541,897 shares valued at about $177 million while selling a small Vista Energy position; and Discovery Capital Management, led by Rob Citrone, increased holdings in YPF to 694,892 shares and Pampa Energía to 77,000 shares while initiating a Vista Energy position of 149,285 shares, bringing its combined sector investment to around $50 million.
items.title: Peter Thiel Expands Investments in Vaca Muerta Oil Exporter

items.summary: A Yogyakarta court sentenced Anita Palupi, principal of the Little Aresha Daycare Centre, to five years in prison and ordered a 510 million rupiah (US$27,900) fine. The ruling came on Thursday (Nov 19) following police raids earlier this year that found dozens of children aged 2 to 6 with their hands and feet bound together. Prosecutors had sought a 10-year term, so the five-year sentence was half what they requested. Judges also ordered Palupi to pay the fine. The daycare centre in Yogyakarta province was raided by police in late April during an investigation that identified 144 child victims while naming 32 suspects overall. Prosecutors alleged that Little Aresha operated without a licence and that caregivers routinely tied up, slapped, and pinched children to make them easier to manage. Reuters could not immediately contact the defendant's legal representatives for comment. In late October, 11 other caregivers were sentenced to prison terms ranging from two to three years, also lighter than prosecutors' demands for five-year terms, and each was fined 60 million rupiah (US$3,285), local media reported. In a separate case, daycare centre chairperson Diyah Kusumastuti is charged with directing the abuse and operating an unlicensed facility from 2022 to 2026; she faces a 10-year prison sentence and a 900 million rupiah fine, as well as 1.2 billion rupiah (US$65,700) in restitution for 83 children, local media reported.
items.title: Yogyakarta court sentences daycare principal to five years over child abuse

items.summary: Un article de recherche examine comment les technologies d'intelligence artificielle appliquées à la santé peuvent involontairement renforcer les inégalités sanitaires existantes en Afrique australe. L'auteur et Shiven Naidoo, doctorant en bioinformatique à l'université du Witwatersrand, ont développé un cadre conceptuel pour analyser comment les populations sont représentées dans les données de santé, comment les algorithmes les classent et hiérarchisent, et comment ces classifications influencent l'accès aux soins. En Afrique du Sud, des unités médicales mobiles utilisent l'IA pour examiner des radiographies thoraciques afin de détecter la tuberculose : une étude rurale dans le KwaZulu-Natal a dépisté près de 10 000 personnes, et un programme national présenté par le Partenariat « Stop TB » en décembre 2024 avait atteint plus de 450 000 personnes grâce à 33 unités mobiles. Au Zimbabwe, une technologie similaire est utilisée dans les communautés minières pour dépister la silicose. Les chercheurs ont constaté que ces systèmes risquent d'aggraver les inégalités dès le stade de la collecte des données : les patients ruraux et peu ressourceux peuvent être sous-représentés en raison d'un accès limité aux soins, de dossiers médicaux incomplets et de systèmes numériques fragmentés. Les infractions sanitaires déconnectées laissent des antécédents incomplets, particulièrement lors d'un changement d'établissement ou de province. Le problème s'étend à la génétique : la plupart des recherches génomiques se sont appuyées sur des données d'ascendance européenne, ce qui rend les outils de prédiction du risque moins précis pour les populations africaines. Les scores de risque polygéniques élaborés principalement à partir de données européennes peuvent être peu performants chez les personnes noires africaines et limiter leur utilité clinique. La surveillance génomique des agents pathogènes dépend des capacités de séquençage, des infrastructures numériques et de l'expertise spécialisée, concentrées dans les grands centres ; par conséquent, les échantillons provenant d'épidémies dans des communautés moins bien équipées peuvent être séquencés tardivement ou pas du tout. Lors de l'épidémie d'Ebola de 2013 à 2016 en Afrique de l'Ouest, une interruption du séquençage a retardé l'analyse de certains échantillons et limité le suivi en temps réel de la propagation virale entre les communautés. Les chercheurs proposent des audits réguliers pour détecter les biais, l'utilisation de données locales plus représentatives, et l'implication des communautés dans la conception et l'évaluation des systèmes. Ils soulignent également que les critères utilisés par les algorithmes peuvent marginaliser les personnes atteintes de maladies rares en intégrant une notion de santé « normale », et qu'une étude publiée en 2019 avait montré comment un algorithme américain sous-estimait les besoins des patients noirs en se basant sur les dépenses de santé, leur attribuant ainsi des scores de risque plus faibles. Les mesures agrégées de vulnérabilité peuvent masquer les différences au sein des communautés : une communauté aux dossiers incomplets peut sembler présenter des besoins moindres, et un centre disposant d'une connexion Internet insuffisante génère des données moins exploitables. Un traitement plus efficace des données disponibles ne suffit pas à combler ces lacunes. Les auteurs concluent que l'équité doit être considérée au même titre que les performances cliniques et les coûts lors de l'adoption des technologies, avec un renforcement de la gouvernance de la recherche en Afrique fondé sur la supervision locale, le consentement inclusif et une utilisation équitable des données. Un traitement plus efficace des données disponibles ne peut, à lui seul, combler ces lacunes.
items.title: Une IA médicale plus intelligente mais des résultats inégaux en Afrique australe

items.summary: US President Donald Trump, Russia's Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping held their first-ever trilateral talks in Shenzhen during the APEC Summit. Beijing stated that the meeting is intended to safeguard world peace, though it has also raised concerns about a potential division of the globe into spheres of influence.
items.title: Trump, Putin and Xi hold first trilateral meeting at APEC Summit

items.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump held an unprecedented trilateral summit Thursday in Shenzhen, China, bringing together leaders of the world's three largest nuclear powers: himself, China's Xi Jinping, and Russia's Vladimir Putin. The meeting took place after the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum concluded. According to Trump's opening remarks, the talks centered on nuclear weapons, the war in Ukraine, and enhanced cooperation among the three nations. Trump framed the leaders as uniquely positioned to discuss reducing the number of nuclear weapons worldwide and lowering the risk that those weapons could ever be used. He also stated that beyond exploring potential reductions between the three countries, they would address cooperation to combat nuclear proliferation across other nations globally.
items.title: Trump hosts trilateral summit with Xi and Putin on nuclear weapons

items.summary: Japan Tobacco will record a ¥1.4 trillion ($8.9 billion) charge after Russian presidential decrees this month placed all seven of its local subsidiaries under temporary administration, stripping the company of management control and removing them from its consolidated accounts. The write-down pushes the cigarette maker into a full-year net loss and slashes its dividend forecast. Japan Tobacco now expects an operating loss of ¥368 billion instead of a ¥1 trillion profit, while revising revenue down by ¥63 billion to ¥3.8 trillion. The company had continued operating in Russia after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine while complying with sanctions, leaving it exposed; Russia accounted for about 10% of group sales and roughly a quarter of adjusted operating profit.
items.title: Japan Tobacco takes $8.9 billion charge after Russia seizure

items.summary: The Danish parliament unanimously approved a security agreement between Denmark, Greenland, and the United States during its second reading on Thursday, with all 109 lawmakers present voting in favor after no debate. The deal permits the United States to build two new military bases on the Arctic island of Greenland and remains in force even if Greenland becomes independent. It was signed in New York on September 22 and supplements a 1951 agreement governing US military presence in the territory, which is an autonomous part of Denmark. Greenland's own parliament had earlier approved the pact by 16 votes to seven abstentions in early November. The agreement also bars countries outside the European Union and NATO from operating in strategic sectors, with the stated aim of preventing China or Russia from gaining influence through investment. Trump has repeatedly asserted that the United States must control Greenland for strategic reasons since returning to office in January 2025, remarks that alarmed Denmark as a NATO ally.
items.title: Denmark Ratifies US-Greenland Security Agreement

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin opened their first trilateral summit on the sidelines of the APEC forum in Shenzhen. Analysts expect the meeting to offer more symbolism than breakthroughs, while critics fear it could carve the world into spheres of influence. Topics expected to come up include Ukraine, the Iran war, nuclear disarmament, and artificial intelligence. Trump and Xi also held one-on-one talks on trade and technology.
items.title: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin Open Trilateral Summit in Shenzhen

items.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese directly addressed Vladimir Putin during his APEC speech hours before a landmark trilateral meeting between US President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen. Looking straight at the Russian leader but not looking up when spoken to, Albanese said: "I say very directly to President Putin: end your war, end it now." He also warned that military conflicts were driving up inflation and straining household budgets through disrupted supply chains. The three leaders then held a roughly 90-minute meeting at Kylin Villa on Thursday evening, standing for a photo without shaking hands before entering the room. Xi called the gathering "groundbreaking," while Trump praised Xi's hosting of APEC as an honour and described meeting Putin likewise as an honour. Trump confirmed Ukraine was on the agenda, noting it had already been discussed with Putin earlier that day, and said both sides would likely want to see the war end. He also attacked the International Criminal Court as "out of control" and straying beyond its jurisdiction, while proposing that the three largest nuclear powers discuss reducing their arsenals. Putin framed Russia, China, and the US as sharing joint responsibility for international peace, citing shared interests in settling regional conflicts including Ukraine, and stressing cooperation on mutual respect, equality, and a balance of interests. The meeting drew comparisons to the 1945 Yalta Conference, prompting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to warn against the leaders carving up spheres of influence or redistributing power without smaller nations' involvement."}{
items.title: Albanese Urges Putin to End Ukraine War as Trump, Xi and Putin Open Historic Trilateral Talks

The International Energy Agency's World Oil Outlook projects that global crude oil demand will reach 106 million barrels per day (mb/d) over the next decade, with India showing the strongest growth at three percent per annum on average to 2035. According to the report, demand increases across nearly all sectors in emerging market and developing economies, led by India's three percent annual growth, followed by Africa at 2.8 percent and Southeast Asia at 1.4 percent. Oil remains the single largest energy source through 2050 as structural declines in China and advanced economies are more than offset by growth in these regions plus rising international aviation demand; the IEA also notes that real oil prices surpass $100 per barrel by 2050.

In its Stated Policies Scenario (STEPS), India leads global oil demand growth, adding 1.3 mb/d to 2035, roughly half of the total increase in emerging market and developing economies. Global oil demand was 102 mb/d in 2025 and is expected to contract in 2026 due to an energy crisis stemming from conflict in the Middle East. Under a Climate Policy Scenario (CPS), global demand rises to 106 mb/d in 2035 and 114 mb/d in 2050.

The average annual increase of 0.4 mb/d through 2035 is primarily driven by growth in petrochemical feedstocks at 0.3 mb/d and aviation at 0.2 mb/d, while demand in most other sectors remains broadly flat or declines. Growth then picks up slightly to an average of 0.5 mb/d per year through 2050, mainly from the expansion of car fleets in emerging market and developing economies outside China, where stringent fuel economy policies are not yet in place and EV charging infrastructure remains limited.

Advanced economy oil demand declines by an average of 0.7 percent per year to 2035, with the European Union seeing the steepest drop as accelerating electric vehicle adoption drives fuel substitution in road transport; this decline is partly offset by growth in the United States from rising petrochemical feedstock requirements and continued mobility demand.

The IEA emphasizes that India's energy needs across sectors are growing fast and set to continue expanding rapidly. In all scenarios, India accounts for more growth in energy demand over the next decade than any other country or region worldwide. The agency notes India is adding over 12,000 cars to its roads every day through the decade, will see a 33 percent rise in built spaces, an additional 200 million air conditioners installed in homes, and surging production of iron, steel and cement; as a result, energy demand grows by 2.5 percent annually to 2035 in the STEPS, triple the global rate. India and Southeast Asia see the largest overall increase in energy needs, followed by Latin America, the Middle East and Africa. Electricity demand in India increases by an average of six percent each year until 2035.

The article was published on November 19, 2026.
items.title: IEA: India to lead global oil demand growth at 3% annually through 2035

Shares of Infosys fell as much as 2.49 per cent to ₹1,081.20 in intraday trade on the National Stock Exchange on Thursday, extending a sharp week-long decline even though the company's subsidiary announced a joint venture with Japanese telecom major NTT Docomo. By 12.16 PM the stock was trading at ₹1,081.20, down ₹27.60 from its previous close of ₹1,108.80; it touched an intraday low of ₹1,073.20, not far above its 52-week low of ₹980.40 hit on September 29. The stock opened at ₹1,096.30 and reached a high of ₹1,097.00 before turning sharply lower, with traded volume standing at 54.51 lakh shares worth ₹589.20 crore.

The stock has been a consistent underperformer: it shed 6.10 per cent in the past week, 4.40 per cent over the past month, and is down 33.67 per cent year-to-date, significantly lagging the Nifty 50's 3.02 per cent year-to-date loss. Its 52-week high of ₹1,728.00 was recorded on February 3.

The sell-off comes despite a business development flagged in pre-market notes: Infosys Singapore, a wholly owned subsidiary, will enter a joint venture with NTT Docomo, one of Japan's leading telecommunications companies. The JV, anchored by NTT Docomo and powered by artificial intelligence, will focus on building a virtual economic ecosystem in the metaverse, integrating real businesses with real-world commerce; Infosys has joined NTT Docomo Playspace, Inc. as a strategic partner. SBI Securities described the development as positive for the medium to long term, noting Japan as a key strategic market for Infosys.

However, broader headwinds overrode the stock-specific positive: the Nifty IT index was down 1.50 per cent at the same time, weighed by a strengthening rupee — typically negative for export-dependent software companies — and global concerns about AI-related valuations. Infosys was the worst performer among Nifty IT constituents, declining 2.46 per cent at the index level. The stock's current P/E stands at 14.62, reflecting significant valuation compression from earlier in the year.

The item was published on November 19, 2026.
items.title: Infosys shares fall intraday despite NTT Docomo metaverse JV

items.summary: Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella said in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer that the company should have detected and contained a software flaw responsible for taking Outlook offline last week. He noted the defect only surfaced under a particular pattern of traffic, added "of course, we should have done the testing before," and argued Microsoft ought to have designed its systems so a failure in one part could be isolated before spreading globally. The outage disrupted email at businesses relying on Outlook for day-to-day communication. Nadella also raised a broader problem facing companies running older infrastructure: AI tools can help engineers identify flaws and develop fixes faster, but each fix still has to be tested and installed, and more frequent updates can make existing systems less stable. He described this as a trade-off software providers face while accelerating patch releases and keeping widely used services online, noting "there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that's unpatchable," citing firmware on chillers and HVAC systems connected to the internet. The interview followed Microsoft's Ignite conference pitch for Copilot as the main interface across its business software; a September overhaul consolidated AI tools into one app and introduced usage-based charges for advanced features, giving Microsoft another revenue source if customers buy fewer licences than it typically sells through per-employee arrangements. Nadella said usage already accounts for a substantial part of Dynamics, which handles sales and enterprise planning functions, and that Copilot can direct requests to models from Anthropic, OpenAI or Microsoft itself as its relationship with OpenAI evolves. On local opposition to data centre construction, he said companies must show residents what they gain, pointing to Quincy, Washington, where Microsoft has operated a data centre for about two decades and tax revenue helped fund a school and other public facilities. He also addressed Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, a major Azure chip supplier, calling Huang a "singular founder" while saying Microsoft remained keen to work with interim chief executive Colette Kress, a former Microsoft employee, leaving Nvidia's board to decide what comes next.
items.title: Nadella says Microsoft should have caught Outlook bug before global outage

items.summary: A series of major technology outages struck over a week in November, prompting lawmakers to demand explanations and leaving users uncertain about the cause. The disruptions affected very different systems: Microsoft's email services went down on November 12 after two days of failures, with Downdetector logging 130,000 reports of Outlook problems at peak; Microsoft traced the failure to a latent software defect in its networking gateway servers worsened by changes in network traffic and reduced server capacity. The next day, around 3:30 pm ET, the Federal Aviation Administration halted all air travel across the US until about 8:30 pm, stranding tens of thousands; the FAA later said a faulty router installed the week before caused the shutdown and has since stopped installing new routers at its telecom sites. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy admitted finding the router took longer than he would have liked and put contractor L3Harris on notice, while officials dismissed rumors that artificial intelligence triggered the outage. On November 16, JPMorgan Chase customers faced delayed transactions due to a software bug in an on-premises hardware system, with Downdetector logging more than 20,000 reports of problems by mid-afternoon; other banks including Truist and Capital One also drew complaints. A day later, Apple reported an outage affecting its App Store, Apple Pay, Apple Music, AppleCare services, and iCloud sign-in after an internal update, with the company saying all platforms had since returned to normal. Beyond these four visible incidents, outages between November 12 and 16 also hit Anthropic's Claude, Workday, AWS's us-east-1 region, United Airlines, Marriott's website and apps, and systems at the National Security Agency. Officials say the incidents appear unrelated with no sign of a coordinated cyberattack, though some causes remain unclear; what they share is dependence on a handful of platforms and legacy networks that let a single fault spread quickly. Separately, Pakistan's telecom regulator said on November 18 that a fault in the SEA-ME-WE 5 undersea cable about 11 km off its coast could cause intermittent connectivity and slower service while traffic was rerouted during an investigation. Lawmakers have called for briefings at federal agencies, the FAA's review of its router failure is continuing, and fuller explanations from Microsoft, Chase, and others may reveal whether the week reflected bad luck or deeper systemic weakness.
items.title: Back-to-Back Tech Outages Raise Reliability Concerns

items.summary: An Instagram advertisement for pistols exposed an illegal firearms trade in Pune, prompting a raid by Wagholi police in the Kesanand area that resulted in three arrests and one detention of a minor. Two of the arrested men had travelled from Goa to Pune to purchase weapons after finalising a deal through social media. Police seized four country-made pistols, four magazines, and 15 live cartridges from the suspects, collectively valued at ₹4,18,500. The identified individuals are Akash alias Gajya Ashok More, 21, of Navratna Society in Vadgaon Sheri; Manish Dilip Fernandes, 26; and Chandreshwar Mallesh, 21, both residents of Chandor in Margao, Goa. A minor was also detained in connection with the case. The operation began after Police Constable Pradeep Mote received a tip-off while patrolling, alerting him that three to four people carrying pistols were waiting on the road toward Jogeshwari Hill. Acting on this information, a team led by Police Sub-Inspector Shivshankar Raghu rushed to the location and detained the suspects. During investigation, police found that More had posted an offer for pistols on Instagram, prompting Fernandes from Goa to contact him and negotiate the purchase; after agreeing, Fernandes and his associate travelled to Kesanand to complete the transaction. Police also reported that More allegedly procured the firearms from Madhya Pradesh and had a prior criminal case registered against him for alleged pistol possession. A case has been filed at Wagholi Police Station under relevant Arms Act provisions, with further investigation underway to establish the weapons' source and identify others in the supply network.
items.title: Instagram Firearms Deal Leads to Pune Arrests

items.summary: Despite an India-UK trade agreement that came into effect in July and reduced tariffs on Scotch whisky from 150% to 75%, a dispute over customs classification has left thousands of litres of bulk Scotch stuck at Indian ports. The disagreement centres on whether bulk Scotch concentrates qualify for the concessional tariff or should be classified as raw material under a newly created category called "compound alcoholic preparations," which attracts a 150% tariff, with an additional consumption tax pushing the effective duty to 162.5%. Indian investigators argue that bulk Scotch is merely a raw material used in manufacturing and therefore does not qualify for reduced tariffs, while liquor companies including Pernod Ricard, Diageo, and Bacardi contend that all Scotch imports should receive the 75% rate regardless of whether they are bottled or brought in bulk. The dispute has left more than 80 shipping containers belonging to these three companies blocked at Indian ports. To secure provisional release while investigations continue, companies can pay duty equivalent to 75% of goods value upfront and cover the remainder through bank guarantees; Pernod Ricard and Diageo have moved to arrange such funding, while Bacardi was still considering its next steps. The arrangement adds pressure on working capital, with smaller manufacturers facing greater difficulties as they may need collateral and must report these guarantees as contingent liabilities. Bulk Scotch imports are central to India's whisky industry, accounting for around 80% of British Scotch imports by volume, most used to produce Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) blended whiskies sold at lower prices than fully imported brands such as Chivas Regal and Johnnie Walker. The UK government has repeatedly stated it is working with New Delhi to resolve the issue, with a spokesperson telling Reuters that ministers were "urgently working with the government of India to resolve this issue." The Scotch Whisky Association estimated 2024 exports stood at $335 million and forecast the trade agreement could increase exports by $1.34 billion over five years.
items.title: India-UK Trade Dispute Blocks Bulk Scotch Whisky Imports

items.summary:
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways revised pollution under control (PUC) certificate rules through the Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, which amend Rule 115(7) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. Notified on November 13 and effective upon publication in the Official Gazette, the amendment replaces a system that set validity primarily by Bharat Stage emission category with one based on vehicle age and whether the vehicle is used privately or commercially. It also standardises testing intervals across states, replacing regional variations.

Under the earlier rules, all private BS-VI vehicles received certificates valid for 12 months regardless of age; commercial BS-VI vehicles likewise had a uniform year-long validity. The new framework introduces three age-based brackets for both categories. For private BS-VI vehicles: up to six years old receive three-year certificates (up from one), those aged more than six and up to ten years keep 12-month validity, and those older than ten years drop to six months. Commercial BS-VI vehicles get shorter extensions; the first bracket rises to two years instead of three, while the middle bracket stays at 12 months and the over-ten-years bracket falls to six months.

For older emission standards, the amendment imposes uniform intervals nationwide: all BS-I, II and III vehicles now require certificates valid for three months regardless of age or category, aligning with Delhi's existing requirement. BS-IV vehicles move from a 12-month central provision to a standard six-month validity across private and commercial use.

The rules also clarify renewal timing: if testing occurs within the ten days before expiry, the renewed certificate takes effect from the previous one's expiry date; if tested on or after expiry, it becomes valid from the test date. Certificates issued before the amendment remain valid until their original expiry dates, and owners need not obtain fresh certificates immediately - new validity applies only at first renewal under the amended rules.

The article notes that all vehicles must hold a certificate from an authorised state testing centre, verifiable digitally through the Parivahan PUCC Portal. It also flags uncertainty: earlier provisions exempted new vehicles across emission categories from obtaining a separate PUC for their first year after registration, but the amendment does not clarify whether this exemption has been retained or altered.
items.title: India shortens and standardises PUC certificate validity by vehicle age

items.summary: The BJP launched a broadside against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Thursday over remarks he made at an event in Chicago. BJP leaders claimed that Rahul had called Indian democracy "sick," but the video released by news agencies showed him instead describing the democracy as "sacred." The exchange occurred during an interaction with students at the University of Chicago, where Rahul was asked why the opposition does not boycott elections if it believes they are being rigged. He responded that their strategy is to expose what is happening and take a beating until people in India realize that the system has been fully demolished. BJP leader Bhandari condemned the remarks, stating that Rahul had again proven he loves his family's party while hating democracy, and called him the "Leader of Anti India Propaganda," arguing that every time Rahul speaks this way he shows himself to be against the Indian state, its people, and its democratic fabric. The article was written by Rohitashwa Ranjan, a digital journalist with The Times of India who covers elections, party dynamics, and politics beneath headlines.
items.title: BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of calling Indian democracy 'sick'

items.summary: On Thursday morning, shares of air-conditioning makers rose as benchmark London Metal Exchange copper contracts fell to their lowest level since April 7. Voltas jumped more than 5% to Rs 1,192.90 apiece on the NSE, while Blue Star surged over 5% to Rs 1,709.10 apiece. PG Electroplast, which supplies components for air conditioners, rose around 6% to trade near Rs 571 apiece. The copper decline followed a stronger US dollar and growing concerns about Chinese industrial demand, with the selloff overshadowed by weakness in AI-linked stocks that had otherwise been tightening copper supply. A stronger dollar was attributed to Federal Reserve meeting minutes suggesting officials saw rising inflation risk while holding rates steady, along with hawkish comments from Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid warning that inflation remained too high and more action may be needed. CME's FedWatch tool priced a nearly 90% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the December FOMC meeting, with a 10% probability of a larger 50-basis-point move. Analysts also linked falling copper to worries about China's economy and its prolonged property downturn, given the metal's heavy use in construction, electrical wiring and infrastructure. The AI-linked stock selloff added pressure as enthusiasm for new data centre spending cooled, even though copper is essential to that electrical infrastructure. Over the past week, Voltas gained 7% and Blue Star jumped 8%, while PG Electroplast recorded marginal weekly losses; over a month, Voltas rose 17%, Blue Star climbed 9% and PG Electroplast jumped 12%. The three stocks delivered returns in the range of 45-150% over three years. Axis Securities noted that FOMC minutes could shape the broader commodities outlook. The article was written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or Investment Adviser and holds no financial interest in the companies mentioned.
items.title: Falling copper prices lift Voltas and other AC stocks

items.summary:
Tamil Nadu faces intensifying climate stress as El Niño is expected to worsen both drought and extreme rainfall risks across the state. The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) confirmed an 80-100% probability of a persistent El Niño phase extending into April 2027, with global warming raising baseline ocean temperatures and amplifying the cycle's effects on already climate-stressed regions like India.

Tamil Nadu relies heavily on monsoon inflows for water security: the southwest monsoon (June to September) replenishes reservoirs while the northeast monsoon (October to December) sustains rainfall. This year's southwest monsoon ended on September 30 with a 12.6% rainfall deficiency, the lowest since 2015, creating deficits over Western Ghats catchment areas and reducing reservoir inflows into Tamil Nadu.

Historically, India experienced 16 El Niño events between 1951 and 2025 lasting nine to 18 months each. Major Indian drought years occurred during strong El Niño periods in 1982, 1987, 2002, 2009, and 2015, with southwest monsoon deficiencies of 14.3% in 2015, 21.8% in 2009, and 19.2% in 2002.

A 52-year climate study (1971-2022) published in the International Journal of Climatology found that south peninsular India, including Tamil Nadu, is prone to drought as a long-term trend. TNAU projects normal northeast monsoon rainfall of 468 mm versus a seasonal average of 464 mm for 2026, offering only partial relief while El Niño may cause uneven distribution with intense coastal rainfall and drier interior conditions.

Agriculture in Tamil Nadu depends on the monsoons, and uneven rainfall makes rainfed systems vulnerable as reduced moisture lowers crop yields. Major crops including paddy, groundnut, maize, cotton, pulses, sugarcane, millets, and coconut are affected, along with livestock facing water stress and fodder shortages.

Districts flagged for El Niño vulnerability cluster in northern and central Tamil Nadu: Ariyalur, Perambalur, Tiruppattur, Vellore, Tiruchirappalli, Cuddalore, Kallakurichi, Kanchipuram, Ranipettai, Tiruvallur, Tiruvannamalai, Villupuram, and Pudukkottai. Agricultural districts draw water from upstream Karnataka, which weakens with a poor southwest monsoon, while interior rainfed areas depend on poorly maintained small reservoirs.

Groundwater remains heavily exploited but depleted; the Central Ground Water Board's 2025 assessment classified 103 of Tamil Nadu's 313 groundwater units as over-exploited. Coastal aquifers across nearly 1,076 kilometres spanning 14 coastal districts face seawater intrusion from sea level rise.

The Tamil Nadu government constituted an expert committee in July under the Disaster Management Act, 2005 to advise TNDRRA on El Niño preparedness. Activist G. Sundarrajan of Poovulagin Nanbargal says these recommendations remain unimplemented and urges restoring water resources "on a war footing." ICAR's District-wise Contingency Plan of 2026 places western and central Tamil Nadu districts in highly to medium vulnerable categories, recommending drought-tolerant crops, rainwater harvesting, soil moisture conservation, and improved irrigation.

Experts note El Niño can also bring intense rainfall causing floods, as seen historically. Akshay Deoras of the University of Reading observed early indications that coastal Tamil Nadu rainfall could improve in November and December 2026.
items.title: El Niño threatens to deepen Tamil Nadu's water stress and agricultural risk

items.summary: The international response to climate change remains inadequate, leaving vulnerable communities to absorb costs from disasters they did little to cause. The Fund for responding to Loss and Damage was created in 2022 after developing countries spent decades demanding financial support for destruction that cannot be prevented through emissions cuts or avoided through adaptation. In its first funding round, the fund received 176 requests from 119 countries seeking a total of $2.8 billion while setting aside only $342 million; an initial package is due before its board in December. Of the $822.71 million pledged by governments recorded in UN documents, just $485.77 million had been received by July 31, and the fund's first replenishment process will not begin until 2027. Harjeet Singh of the Fill the Fund campaign called it "a lifeboat with no oars," arguing that a few hundred million dollars in voluntary pledges cannot match the scale of destruction and that vulnerable countries need large-scale grants rather than loans that deepen debt. Nepal illustrates the gap: August floods from a glacier collapse killed more than 1,400 people, and while the World Bank estimates recovery will cost about $4.8 billion, the fund has provisionally set aside just $21.6 million, which is not yet disbursed money. Delays compound the problem because countries must prepare proposals and wait for approvals before funds are released, costing families shelter and farmers lost seasons. The urgency is acute in South Asia: Pakistan's Sindh province farmers remain dealing with 2022 floods that destroyed crops and homes; coastal Bangladesh faces saltwater intrusion, storm surges and erosion affecting health, culture and social ties; India confronts similar pressures along its coast, including the Sundarbans. On Pari Island near Jakarta, around 4,000 people live on just over 41 hectares after worsening tidal flooding since 2019 with a worst point in 2021. Four residents sued cement producer Holcim for compensation and emission reduction; the case was declared admissible in 2025 but the company has appealed, though liability remains unestablished. For Pacific islanders, rising seas threaten freshwater sources and places central to identity: Kirsten Madison of the Marshall Islands said land holds identities, languages and traditions, while Harjeet Singh added that existence cannot be put a price tag on. The fund can help families rebuild homes, farmers recover livelihoods and countries protect communities from repeated shocks, but it cannot restore lost land or replace uprooted cultures; this requires substantially more money, faster decisions and easier access to grants as negotiations continue in Antalya.
items.title: Climate loss and damage fund falls far short of needs

items.summary: At a CBT meeting reported by ANI, EPFO discussed approving a systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) for employees' provident fund members. Under the current rules, a member retiring at age 58 after at least 10 years of service can withdraw 100% of their corpus and claim a monthly EPS pension. The SWP proposal would let retirees instead receive payouts every month while keeping the rest of their savings within the EPF ecosystem earning interest at 8.25%. Members could choose to withdraw funds on a monthly, quarterly, or annual basis without surrendering ownership of the residual corpus. In the event of death during the payout period, the nominee or dependent would be able to either withdraw the remaining balance or continue receiving periodic payments. EPFO stated that the initiative aims to enhance retirement financial security by providing members with a flexible, regular and reliable income stream while safeguarding families' interests. The plan is aimed at retirees and would initially cover existing subscribers; EPFO estimates suggest about 6.3 crore members above age 55 could benefit in the initial phase. According to internal EPFO estimates reported by TOI, people choosing SWP over bank fixed deposits or annuities would receive bigger returns on their retirement corpus because the remaining funds continue earning interest and compounding while offering income tax benefits. Alongside the SWP discussion, EPFO eased minimum PF balance requirement rules, reducing them from 25% to 10%, allowing members to withdraw up to 90% of savings before age 55. The CBT also cut the waiting period for employees to withdraw their PF savings from 12 months to just 2 months, while the minimum waiting period for final pension withdrawal remains unchanged at 36 months.
items.title: EPF SWP proposal allows retirees monthly withdrawals while retaining corpus

items.summary: The Bombay high court directed Bank of Baroda to maintain a status quo over documents requested by Bavaguthu Raghuram Shetty in his $15 billion lawsuit against the lender. The direction followed allegations that bank officials participated in fraud at Shetty's company, NMC Healthcare, and came after his counsel sought immediate inspection of records held by the bank, including loan guarantees believed to establish the lender's role in the disputed transactions. Senior counsel Birendra Saraf argued on behalf of the bank that there was no reason to expect destruction of the records, noting that related proceedings were also underway in Abu Dhabi; the bank assured the court it would preserve the documents unaltered until a hearing scheduled for 17 December. Shetty's lawyer contended that transferring such a massive sum from NMC Healthcare required involvement from Bank of Baroda officials at its Abu Dhabi branch and pointed to approximately 150 alerts generated by the bank's system regarding suspicious money laundering transactions, which he said were all closed without investigation. A single-judge bench headed by Justice Arif S. Doctor declined immediate disclosure and ordered that status quo be maintained over the documents listed in Shetty's application. Separately, on 29 October, Shetty filed two interim applications requesting court-monitored forensic preservation of electronic records along with disclosure of relevant bank communications, transaction data, emails, and banking system records, while also asking for a commissioner to inspect and preserve these materials. In his second application he sought an order directing the bank to set aside the claimed amount in a reserve unavailable for distribution, arguing that failure to do so could later be used by the bank to resist payment of any award. Shetty, founder of NMC Healthcare and UAE Exchange, accuses Bank of Baroda and its officials of helping former executives move money out of the group; his suit names 26 defendants including former NMC executives Prasanth Manghat and Promoth Manghat, and seeks $15 billion in damages covering financial losses and reputational harm plus 18% annual interest.
items.title: Bombay HC maintains status quo on Bank of Baroda records sought by Shetty

items.summary:
A controversy has erupted over a Karthigai Deepam lamp ritual on Thiruparankundram hill near Madurai, Tamil Nadu. For centuries the hill and the Sri Subramaniya Swamy Temple at its foothills hosted shared worship across Hindu sects, Jainism, Buddhism, Islam, and Saivism. Certain Hindu groups now claim ownership of the entire hill despite a 13th century Sikandar Badshah dargah and Jain relics being present there. The State's Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department has lit a deepam on a Nayak-era stone pillar near Uchi Pillayar Koil every year for over 100 years, without interruption.

Some Hindu outfits obtained an order from single judge G.R. Swaminathan of the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court allowing them to light the deepam instead on a plain granite pillar about 30 meters away near the dargah. The judge ruled that pillar stood on temple property, later upheld by a two-member bench; he also sent a Central Industrial Security Force battalion to protect petitioners and initiated contempt proceedings against district officials for non-compliance. In a January 6, 2026 ruling, Justices G. Jayachandran and K.K. Ramakrishnan of the Madurai Bench upheld Swaminathan's order but directed that no general public access be allowed on the hill during next year's festival.

The State government argued the judge overstepped his brief by threatening centuries-old peace among faiths, risking law-and-order problems with thousands already gathered. It recorded strong resentment at the CISF deployment as unprecedented interference in its internal affairs and said it had no alternative but to bar public access that day; the festival passed off peacefully.

Experts say lighting the deepam on the Uchi Pillayar Koil pillar follows Agama Shastras, per a December 6, 1995 statement by hereditary priests (Sthaneeka Bhattars) who said their ancestors lit it there since time immemorial. The hill holds archaeological and cultural significance from the 2nd century CE onward: early Sangam-era Murugan worship, rock-cut cave temples attributed to Pallava and Pandiya periods around the 3rd to 6th centuries, Jain monks taking over afterward, and restored Murugan and Shiva worship during the Bhakti movement. The Nayak regime expanded the temple with stone mandaps; King Veerappa Naicker built the main tower in 1583.

The disputed pillar near the dargah is a plain granite column bearing no carvings or inscriptions, unlike the Hanuman-carved Nayak-era deepathoon. Art historian T. Gandhirajan speculates it may have been a be vilakku thandu lamppost guiding travellers on the ancient Madurai-Kochi Peru Vazhi, with small dents to hold about 500 ml of oil; he notes any genuine temple deepathoon would carry historical and religious carvings. The State has refuted claims that it is a Jain lamp pillar or survey marker.

The hill spans 172.2 acres at 1048 feet, with two peaks: a smaller southern peak and a taller northern one topped by the dargah. Certain portions on the western side are under the Archaeological Survey of India, where Jain sculptures and stone beds appear. A 1923 Madura subordinate court ruling held that the entire hill except cultivated assessed lands and the mosque site belonged to the Murugan Temple; the dargah's property included Nellithope with a few graves plus its flagstaff and steps. The London Privy Council agreed in 1931, and post-Independence Madras High Court judgments upheld these rulings while emphasising status quo of worship rights under the Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act of 1991.

The hill also hosts two survey stations of the Great Trigonometrical Survey's Southern Trigon. The first station, established in 1806-07 and recorded as Sikandarmalai, lay about 53 yards south-southeast near the dargah; a second station marked by an engraved circle and dot was set up in 1871 on the northwestern side of the summit. Litigation dates back to 1862, settled in the 1920s, rekindled in 1978 and again in 2025; in October 2025 the Madras High Court banned animal sacrifice at the dargah and affirmed temple ownership except for 0.33 acres around the dargah and Nellithope.

The political fallout included a DMK impeachment motion against Judge Swaminathan in Parliament, with Tamil Nadu's government left only to approach the Supreme Court if it feels wronged; analysts warn reviving this settled dispute threatens peaceful coexistence and may shape future politics in Tamil Nadu.
items.title: Thiruparankundram deepam controversy and its legal fallout

items.summary: On Thursday, November 19, Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta led a post-Chhath Puja cleanliness drive at the Munak Nehar ghat in Shalimar Bagh, joined by Bollywood personalities including Jackie Shroff, Esha Gupta, Stebin Ben, and singer Bismil. The event followed Chhath celebrations held on November 15 and 16 across roughly 1,400 ghats where devotees offered arghya to the Sun God along an 11-kilometre stretch of the Munak Canal. According to a statement from the chief minister's office (CMO), the drive aimed to promote environmental protection, cleanliness, and public participation. Gupta described keeping Delhi clean as the collective responsibility of residents and asserted that festivals must always be followed by cleanup efforts. In footage posted by ANI, she removed her shoes and entered the water to remove scrap and discarded materials from the ghat steps. The CMO noted that prominent participants gave the campaign special recognition and helped spread its environmental message more widely. Gupta also praised the involvement of schoolchildren and youth, framing the effort as extending beyond Munak Canal to encompass all of Delhi and the Yamuna River, with public participation adding momentum to keep the city green and pristine.
items.title: Delhi CM leads post-Chhath cleanliness drive at Munak Canal with celebrities

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, alongside Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, attended the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers' Dialogue in Tokyo on Thursday. Addressing the media after the meeting, Jaishankar warned that connectivity, resources, services, supply chains and market shares were increasingly being weaponised, with many of these trends carrying direct implications for national security; he stressed that strengthening resilience and exploring new options must be viewed through this lens. He placed these remarks within a global order facing multiple shocks, including two major ongoing conflicts whose effects have reached distant regions, economic volatility, and the after-effects of COVID-19, which together heightened concerns over energy, trade, food and health security. Jaishankar said New Delhi and Tokyo remain committed to keeping the Indo-Pacific free and open, joined by other Quad partners, and noted that old assumptions may no longer hold as each country must make a greater contribution to global good through national, bilateral or like-minded partnerships. He highlighted growing concerns over connectivity and chokepoints in light of Gulf experiences, emphasising the importance of ensuring maritime trade functions smoothly while both sides agreed on adhering to international law. The dialogue also addressed the changing nature of warfare, with Jaishankar pointing to the effective use of smart weapons and innovative solutions that feed into broader India-Japan engagement on innovation and startups. He framed the wider objective as supporting a multipolar Asia and world through reformed multilateralism, describing the two nations' long history of friendship and goodwill. The 2+2 format convenes both countries' foreign and defence ministers to review their strategic relationship and discuss regional and global security challenges. These remarks followed a Quad leaders' summit in Manila on Tuesday involving Prime Minister Narendra Modi, US President Donald Trump, Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi and Australian PM Anthony Albanese. On Wednesday at the Raisina Tokyo Dialogue, Jaishankar had identified five defining features of the changing global landscape: repeated shocks to the international system, weaponisation of economic activity, greater risk-taking, de-risking and diversification, and growing importance of trusted partnerships.
items.title: Jaishankar flags weaponisation of resources at India-Japan 2+2 talks

items.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways revised the renewal schedule for Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates on Thursday, making validity depend on a vehicle's emission standard, age, and whether it is used privately or commercially. The changes extend validity for newer vehicles while retaining shorter periods for older ones. BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles will have PUC certificates valid for three months, whereas BS-IV vehicles receive six months of validity. For private BS-VI vehicles, the schedule varies by age: those up to six years old get certificates valid for three years; vehicles aged over six but up to 10 years must renew annually; and those older than 10 years require renewal every six months. Transport (commercial) vehicles follow a slightly different framework under which commercial BS-VI vehicles up to six years old receive two-year validity, while those between six and 10 years of age renew annually and those over 10 years renew every six months. The revised rules differentiate certificate validity based on both emission standards and vehicle age, offering longer periods for newer BS-VI vehicles while keeping shorter renewal cycles for older cars and earlier-standard models. The changes come amid growing concerns about vehicular emissions contributing to air pollution in several Indian cities, including Delhi's ongoing severe air quality crisis.
items.title: India revises PUC certificate validity rules

items.summary: The Odisha government has stepped up precautionary measures ahead of Cyclone 'Akvan', which is projected to cross the coast between Gopalpur and Puri on Friday. Chief Secretary Anu Garg said 9,299 cyclone shelters have been set up across potentially affected districts, over 1 lakh people—specifically 1,05,304—have been evacuated so far into 1,224 cyclone and flood shelters, and 305 emergency response teams are deployed. Priority is being placed on ensuring 'zero casualties'. Tourists have been barred from coastal areas including Gopalpur, Puri, Satapada and Chilika, while fishermen have been prohibited from venturing into the sea; those who had already set out reportedly returned, with coordination underway with the Indian Coast Guard. The state has closed educational institutes in districts under 'red', 'orange' and 'yellow' warnings, cancelled leave for government officials across all districts, deployed senior IAS officers with cyclone experience to likely-affected areas, arranged cooked food, dry rations, essential medicines, drinking water and sanitary napkins at shelters, shifted pregnant women near term to nearby health centres, and prepared helicopters and cranes if needed. Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said 941 locations in five districts have been identified as vulnerable to landslides, with people from hilltop and foothill villages being moved to safety; the Telecommunications Department is providing additional satellite phones and mobile units where connectivity has failed. The Odisha Forest Development Corporation deployed 100 teams to address possible road blockages. Rescue teams are stationed in Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Kalahandi, Gajapati, Ganjam, Kandhamal, Boudh, Puri, Nayagarh and Khurda districts. The IMD's morning bulletin projected the system would cross north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to east of Gopalpur, by Friday noon with maximum sustained winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph; at 8.30 am it was centred about 420 km east-southeast of Narsapur, 400 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam, 490 km south of Gopalpur and 550 km south of Puri, having moved northwards at 15 kmph over the past six hours. A storm surge of 0.5 to 1 metre above astronomical tide is expected in low-lying areas of Ganjam and Puri districts. The chief secretary noted that evacuation figures continue to rise as the process proceeds. Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Director Manorama Mohanty said light to moderate rain has been falling since Wednesday night, with intensity increasing gradually as the system nears the coast; IMD squally winds of 40-50 kmph gusting up to 60 kmph are currently prevailing across south Odisha. Railway authorities cancelled two trains between Visakhapatnam and Koraput on Thursday and Friday.
items.title: Odisha braces for Cyclone Akvan with mass evacuations and shelter preparations
